nodes.label: Variant Consistency vs Vocabulary Size Chart
nodes.norm_label: variant consistency vs vocabulary size chart
nodes.rationale: Line chart of variant consistency (mean Jaccard) vs vocabulary size (1k, 4k, 8k, 16k, log x-axis) for BPE and WordPiece tokenizers. Consistency drops as vocab grows: WordPiece ~0.136 -> 0.071 -> 0.069 -> 0.059; BPE ~0.097 -> 0.066 -> 0.059 -> 0.049. WordPiece is above BPE at every size, and the gap is largest at 1k. Larger vocabularies tokenize spelling variants into less overlapping subword sets.

nodes.label: Continued Words Chart (BPE vs WordPiece)
nodes.rationale: Line chart: % of words split into 2+ tokens vs vocabulary size (1k, 4k, 8k, 16k; log x-axis). Both tokenizers fall steeply as vocab grows: BPE ~43.3% -> 23.6% -> 15.8% -> 10.3%; WordPiece ~47.4% -> 26.0% -> 17.3% -> 11.4%. WordPiece fragments words slightly more than BPE at every size, and the gap narrows as vocab grows (about 4 points at 1k, 1 point at 16k). Diminishing returns past 8k.

nodes.label: Fertility vs Vocabulary Size Chart
nodes.rationale: Line chart of fertility (tokens per word) against vocabulary size (1k, 4k, 8k, 16k; log x-axis) for BPE and WordPiece. Fertility falls monotonically with vocab size: BPE 1.68->1.32->1.20->1.13, WordPiece 1.81->1.36->1.23->1.14. BPE is consistently lower (more efficient); the gap is largest at 1k (~0.12) and nearly vanishes at 16k (~0.01). Diminishing returns beyond 4k.

nodes.label: Macro F1 vs Vocabulary Size Chart
nodes.norm_label: macro f1 vs vocabulary size chart
nodes.rationale: Line chart of classification Macro F1 (%) against subword vocabulary size (1k, 4k, 8k, 16k; log x-axis) for BPE and WordPiece tokenizers, with a dashed word-level baseline at ~63.1%. Both tokenizers score ~59% at 1k and jump to ~63% at 4k. WordPiece peaks at 4k (~63.4%) then declines (63.1 at 8k, 62.6 at 16k); BPE dips at 8k (~62.6) and peaks at 16k (~63.3). Only WordPiece@4k and BPE@16k beat the word-level baseline, and only slightly. Takeaway: vocab >=4k is required; beyond that, subword tokenization gives roughly baseline-level Macro F1.
